findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key crashes on datetime keys
findings.body: `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key()` does `int(math.floor(value) ...)` on the raw attribute value, which only works for numeric keys. The only caller (`OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint`) passes `order_by="-datetime"`, so `value` is a `datetime` and `math.floor(datetime)` raises `TypeError: must be real number, not datetime`. `build_cursor()` always invokes `key=self.get_item_key` on the results, so any request with `optimized_pagination=true` that returns at least one row will 500. The class should subclass/reuse `DateTimePaginator`'s key handling (or at minimum not be wired to a datetime-ordered queryset).

findings.title: value_from_cursor returns raw int for a datetime column
findings.body: `OptimizedCursorPaginator.value_from_cursor()` returns `cursor.value` unchanged (integer/float), but `BasePaginator.build_queryset()` injects it into a raw SQL `WHERE "datetime" <= %s` clause. Since the endpoint orders by `-datetime`, the value must be converted back to a `datetime` as `DateTimePaginator.value_from_cursor()` does. As written, following any cursor will either raise a database type error or silently compare a timestamp column against an integer, returning wrong pages. Additionally, cursor values produced by `DateTimePaginator` (milliseconds) and this paginator are not interchangeable, so a client toggling `optimized_pagination` between requests will feed incompatible cursors to the other paginator.

findings.title: Negative slice on a QuerySet raises ValueError, not supported by Django
findings.body: In the `enable_advanced_features and cursor.offset < 0` branch, `start_offset` (and often `stop`) are negative and used as `queryset[start_offset:stop]`. Django's `QuerySet.__getitem__` explicitly raises `ValueError("Negative indexing is not supported.")` for negative slice bounds, so the comment claiming "the underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically" is false. Since `offset` comes straight from the user-supplied `cursor` query parameter (`Cursor.from_string` accepts negative integers), any authorized caller can trigger an unhandled 500 by sending e.g. `cursor=0:-1:0` with `optimized_pagination=true`. Negative offsets should be rejected with `BadPaginationError` instead.

findings.title: Silently clamping negative offsets masks invalid cursors and is inconsistent for prev cursors
findings.body: `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` changes `BasePaginator.get_result()` for every paginator in the codebase: a forward cursor with a negative offset, which previously surfaced an error, now silently returns the first page as if the cursor were `offset=0`, while the cursors returned in the response are built from the original negative `cursor.offset` (see `_build_next_values`/`_build_prev_values`), producing inconsistent/incorrect next/prev links. For `is_prev` cursors the negative offset is still passed through and will raise Django's `ValueError: Negative indexing is not supported.` (a 500) rather than a `BadPaginationError`. Negative offsets should be validated and rejected explicitly in one place.

findings.title: Extra-row trimming uses raw offset instead of the slice offset
findings.body: The check `elif len(results) == offset + limit + extra:` compares the number of fetched rows against the un-clamped `offset`, but the rows were fetched with `start_offset` (which can differ from `offset` after clamping or in the negative-offset branch). When they differ, the extra look-ahead row is not dropped, so a previous-page response can contain `limit + 1` items / an item that belongs to the adjacent page. Use `start_offset` consistently (same issue exists in the `BasePaginator` copy at line 192).

findings.title: organization_context.member can be None -> AttributeError 500
findings.body: `enable_advanced = request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access` dereferences `organization_context.member` unconditionally when the requester is not a superuser. For requests authenticated with an org API key/auth token (or any caller that passes `OrganizationAuditPermission` without being a member), `member` is `None`, so this raises `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'has_global_access'` and the endpoint returns a 500 for every GET, not just optimized ones. Guard with `organization_context.member is not None` and only evaluate the flag when `use_optimized` is actually requested.

findings.title: "admin-only" gate is actually satisfied by any member of an open-membership org
findings.body: The comment says the optimized path is enabled only for "authorized administrators", but the condition uses `member.has_global_access`, which is true for every member of an organization with open membership (and for any member whose role grants global access), not just admins/owners. Combined with the new unvalidated negative-offset path in `OptimizedCursorPaginator`, this lets ordinary members reach code that bypasses the normal offset bounds and crashes the request. If this is meant to be admin-only, check the actual role/permission (e.g. superuser or `org:admin`); the claim that "permissions are checked at the queryset level" in paginator.py is also unsupported for this path.

findings.title: New paginator and endpoint branch have no tests
findings.body: `OptimizedCursorPaginator` (including the negative-offset branch) and the new `optimized_pagination=true` endpoint branch are added with no unit or API tests. Given that the class as written raises `TypeError` on datetime keys and `ValueError` on negative slices, even a single test exercising the new query parameter would have caught the breakage. Tests should cover: optimized path with/without a cursor, negative offsets, and unauthorized callers falling back to `DateTimePaginator`.

findings.title: Misleading comment documents negative offsets as a supported feature
findings.body: The added comment states that `Cursor` now "allows negative offsets for advanced pagination scenarios", but no behavior changed here (offsets were never validated) and downstream consumers cannot handle negative offsets: Django querysets reject negative slice bounds and `OffsetPaginator`/`ChainPaginator` explicitly raise `BadPaginationError("Pagination offset cannot be negative")`. Documenting an unsupported, user-controllable value as a feature invites more code to rely on it; either add real validation here or drop the comment.
